title: The Charity Bake Sale
story:
Students at West Hill School held a bake sale for the town clinic. Hana brought a lemon cake, and Oscar brought bags of cookies. They set two tables in the hall and wrote the prices on cards. A slice of cake cost two euros, and a bag of cookies cost one euro. Their teacher said the goal was eighty euros.

By noon the cookies were selling quickly, but the cake was selling slowly. A younger pupil wanted a slice and had only one euro. Hana looked at the quiet table and chose to lower the cake price for the last hour. She crossed out the old number and wrote one euro on the card. Oscar worried that the class would miss the goal.

At the end of the day they counted the cash box. The cookies had brought forty-six euros. The cake had brought thirty-nine euros. The total was eighty-five euros. The lower price had brought more buyers, so the cake earned more than Oscar expected. Parents bought extra bags on the way out of school. Hana kept a list so the class could see the total grow. The class put the notes and coins into an envelope for the clinic. The next morning the clinic sent a short letter of thanks. Oscar admitted that the new price had been a good idea. The students decided to hold another sale before the winter holiday.
